outcome: The general conjecture remains open, but Dalal, McDonald and Shan (arXiv:2405.07382, posted 12 May 2024; published Journal of Graph Theory 110(3):249-262, 2025) proved a new general upper bound χ_T(G) ≤ Δ(G)+2⌈|V(G)|/(Δ(G)+1)⌉ for every finite simple graph (improving Hind's 1992 bound by one color), and used it to confirm the conjecture outright — χ_T(G) = Δ(G)+2 — for a class of sufficiently large, sufficiently dense r-regular graphs (r ≥ (1+ε)n/2). A related 2025 preprint (Henderschedt, McDonald, Shan, arXiv:2507.05548) extends the dense-regular result to large minimum degree rather than regularity.
summary: The general Total Coloring Conjecture (χ_T(G) ≤ Δ(G)+2 for every finite simple graph) remains open. Since the frozen revision date, the substantive development is Dalal, McDonald and Shan's paper 'Total Coloring Graphs With Large Maximum Degree' (arXiv:2405.07382, first posted 12 May 2024, published in Journal of Graph Theory 110(3):249-262 in 2025 — a peer-reviewed venue, so this passes the 'digested by experts' bar). It (a) improves the best known general bound by one color over Hind's 1992 result, and (b) fully confirms the conjecture (proves the exact Δ(G)+2 bound, not just an upper bound) for a restricted class: r-regular graphs on n vertices with n large and r ≥ (1+ε)n/2 for any fixed ε>0. Part (b) is a genuine case of the stated conjecture settled — dense regular graphs are a restriction of 'every graph' — so this record is coded 'partial' with resolution_direction 'confirmed'. A follow-up 2025 preprint (arXiv:2507.05548, Henderschedt/McDonald/Shan, not yet independently confirmed as journal-published) extends the settled case to large minimum degree instead of regularity, which is the same kind of contribution and does not change the classification. Separately, the 2020 Murthy preprint (arXiv:2003.09658) claiming a full proof of the general conjecture remains unaccepted as of its June 2021 v3 and September 2026: no retraction notice was found, but no journal acceptance, expert digestion, or citation as settled was found either — it continues to be treated as open by these 2024-2025 papers themselves, consistent with the triage's assessment. I found no AI system anywhere in this line of work: the papers are standard combinatorial/probabilistic arguments (degree/regularity conditions, no mention of computer search, SAT solvers, or machine learning in any accessible page or abstract).
competing_reading: One could argue the dense-regular-graph result is closer to a 'related problem' (an asymptotic density condition rather than a natural sub-case named in the literature) and should be scored 'progress' rather than 'partial', since the density/large-n threshold is somewhat artificial and no one graph or finite family is exhibited. But because the theorem proves the exact conjectured bound (not just a weaker bound) for an actual, non-empty subclass of graphs satisfying the stated hypothesis (Δ(G) as maximum degree, over all finite simple graphs), it reads as a genuine case settled rather than a different question, so 'partial' is the better fit.
what_would_settle_it: A resolution (or explicit counterexample) for the fully general conjecture with no density, degree, or regularity restriction; alternatively, expert acceptance (citation as proved, or journal publication) of the 2020 Murthy preprint would change its status from unaccepted claim to resolved/claimed.
